$comment: Mapping between Azure DevOps and Jira. Edit this to match your project. Run `deno task fields` to see the real issue types / statuses / custom fields of the target Jira project.
$comment_issueType: ADO Epic -> Jira Epic; Feature and User Story -> Story. During the hierarchy phase a child whose ADO parent is an Epic is linked through the Epic Link field; any other parent-child pair Jira cannot nest (e.g. Task under a Feature/Story) becomes a 'Relates' link. labels.fromWorkItemType keeps the original ADO type visible.
$comment_status: Only statuses that exist in SWAIS. The project runs more than one workflow, so a mapping applies only to the issue types whose workflow contains that status; anything unreachable keeps its default and is reported at the end of the run.
$comment_sprintDates: CSV source only — a CSV carries no iteration dates. The key is the full Iteration Path.

fields.$comment: Fill in the matching customfield_xxxxx. Leave null when the project has no such field and the tool will skip it. On Jira Server / Data Center, epicLink is required for real Epic hierarchy and epicName is required to create Epics at all.

components.$comment: Map an Area Path (the part after the project name) onto a Jira component name. The component must already exist.

users.$comment: Map an ADO uniqueName/email onto a Jira accountId (Cloud), username (Server), or email. Leave empty to let the tool look users up by email. Set autoLookup to false if the site disables user search.
